newsitem.title: UK: Bradford wool market ruffled by sterling.
newsitem.headline: Bradford wool market ruffled by sterling.

text.p: Tops prices were generally unchanged in Bradford although finest Supers gained a slight three pence per kg, market sources said.
Traders said the market had been ruffled by sterling's fluctuations against the U.S dollar and other primary market currencies.
The renewed strength of the Aussie was said to be behind the pick-up in finer tops values.
"Buyers (in the blended sector) seem wary of moving in at the moment, as sterling could yet push imported wool costs down," one said.
Topmakers working exclusively with homegrown wools are benefitting from healthier consumer demand in the UK, shown in consistently firm prices for English types.
There were few reports of new business and confidence across the sector remains extremely mixed.
